correction: The DONE status stands: the snapshot no longer runs git. The auditor was wrong to report no fix defects. #710 changed Agent Control project plans so the approved 'before' identity comes from the persisted column, but revalidation still checks it against a live git resolve. The two sources now disagree in reachable cases. The worst is a project whose root is missing: its last persisted identity is kept on purpose, while the live resolve returns null. Agent Control can then never update or remove that project, including re-rooting it after the folder moved. Before #710 both sides came from the same resolver cache.
summary: The finding is fixed. Shell snapshots, placement and project lookups read repository_identity_json from projection_projects (migration 086) with no git and no timeout. resolveRepositoryIdentitiesForProjects and timeoutOption(1000) are gone. A background sync with concurrency 4 runs at startup, every 30 min, and on project.created or a root move. It revalidates with stat-only fingerprints of the enclosing repo's commondir/config, forces a re-resolve after 24 h, runs git in the background process lane, and announces changes with an empty project.meta.update that keeps updatedAt. The 1-minute resolver TTLs now back only the stream-enrichment fallback, the sync's refresh, and Agent Control. One regression came in with the fix: AgentControlProjectPlans compares the persisted identity key (stateFor via readWorkspacePlacement) with a live resolver key in revalidate. Agent Control project update/remove fails as 'project-stale: The approved repository identity changed' whenever the persisted identity lags or the root is missing. A lag lasts up to 30 min after a remote change, or seconds for a new or moved project. A missing root never recovers.

evidence.note: buildShell is pure SQL, and the comment says identities are persisted so a snapshot never waits on git. The file only imports decodePersistedRepositoryIdentity (line 73), not the resolver.
getWorkspacePlacement maps project rows with the persisted identity. Agent Control reads this through readWorkspacePlacement.
getProjectShellById uses the persisted identity. The pre-fix code called repositoryIdentityResolver.resolve here (f1be4abc7 lines 2806 and 2837).
Adds the repository_identity_json, _fingerprint and _checked_at columns. There is no backfill: a NULL checked_at means the first sweep resolves the project.

The projector upsert keeps the identity columns unless workspace_root changed. recordRepositoryIdentity only writes when the root still matches, so a race with a move cannot store an identity for the old root.
The stat-only fingerprint walks up to the enclosing .git and follows gitdir/commondir to config size and mtime. It returns null for a missing root.

A null fingerprint (missing root) is skipped, so the last known identity is kept indefinitely. Lines 108-113 skip git when the fingerprint is unchanged and the identity is under 24 h old. Line 117 runs git in the background lane.
A changed identity is announced with an empty project.meta.update. decider.ts:655 keeps updatedAt for an update that changes nothing.
runRepositoryIdentitySync is started after the gate, with the domain-event subscription. It sweeps once immediately, then every 30 min.
project.created and project.meta-updated enrichment reads the persisted identity and calls resolver.resolve only when it is null. This is on the event path, not the snapshot path.
stateFor uses project.repositoryIdentity, the persisted value from readWorkspacePlacement, as the plan's before/expected repositoryIdentityKey (lines 194 and 219).

Regression: revalidate compares the live resolver key (identityKey, git with a 1-min cache) with expected.repositoryIdentityKey, which is persisted. For a missing root, live is null (an unspawnable probe reads as no identity, RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:111) while persisted keeps the old key, so this always fails. After a remote change, persisted lags for up to 30 min. Before #710 both sides came from the resolver (f1be4abc7 used getShellSnapshot with resolver-backed identities).
The test double resolver always returns null and the projects have no persisted identity, so the mismatch is not covered.

fixDefects: AgentControlProjectPlans mixes identity sources since #710. The before/expected repositoryIdentityKey comes from the persisted column (stateFor via readWorkspacePlacement, AgentControlProjectPlans.ts:69/194/219), but revalidate checks it against a live git resolve (AgentControlProjectPlans.ts:266). Three cases follow. (1) The project root is missing, for example an agent ran `mv` and then proposed a project update to the new root, or it wants to unlink a project whose folder was deleted. The sync keeps the last persisted identity (repositoryIdentitySync.ts:104) while the live probe returns null, so update and remove always fail with 'project-stale: The approved repository identity changed', and retrying does not help. (2) After `git remote add/set-url`, persisted lags the live identity for up to 30 min (the sweep interval), so update/remove fails for that long, depending on whether the 1-min resolver cache already holds the new value. (3) Briefly after a project is created or moved, persisted is NULL until the event-triggered sync records it. This sync can sit behind a running sweep's lock. Agent Control project update/remove is the only consumer that compares identities; the snapshot fix itself is sound.
implementationSketch: In apps/server/src/agentControl/Layers/AgentControlProjectPlans.ts, compare like with like by binding approvals to the live identity, as before #710. Change stateFor to take the identity key as an argument. In prepareUpdate and prepareRemove, compute `const currentKey = yield* identityKey(project.workspaceRoot)` and build before/expected with it. In revalidate, compute the live key of current.workspaceRoot once. Compare title, workspaceRoot and updatedAt from the projection, compare the live key against expected.repositoryIdentityKey, and drop the persisted-identity equality at line 261. This keeps the TOCTOU guarantee: the repository identity the user approved is re-checked live at execution. Two alternatives: resolve both sides through resolver.refresh to bypass the 1-min cache, or have prepare trigger the identity sync for that project so persisted and live converge. The live-vs-live comparison is simpler. Tests in AgentControlProjectPlans.test.ts: (a) the persisted identity is null or stale while the resolver returns key K; prepareUpdate/prepareRemove followed by revalidate succeeds. (b) The persisted identity is K, the root is missing, and the resolver returns null; prepareRemove followed by revalidate succeeds. (c) The resolver returns K at prepare and K2 at revalidate; revalidate fails with project-stale. No contract or schema change is needed, because AgentControlProjectState.repositoryIdentityKey only changes provenance.
decisionReason: The snapshot fix needs no decision. The defect fix touches Agent Control approval revalidation. It restores the pre-#710 semantics, where the approved and re-checked identity both come from the live resolver, and does not loosen the post-approval check, so no product or security decision should be needed. A reviewer familiar with Agent Control approvals should still look at it.
